```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(MixSIARPFN)
ok <- MixSIARPFN:::networks_ready()   # the code needs the networks (see pfn_networks())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ok,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
# Inline numbers, only when the code ran
num <- function(x, digits = 2) if (ok) format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits) else "?"
```

This follows MixSIAR's wolves example (Semmens et al. 2009 data, as analysed in Stock
et al. 2018): 66 wolves from 8 packs in 3 regions, whose diet is a mix of deer,
marine mammals and salmon, measured with two tracers (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N). Pack is a random effect nested within the random effect
Region, and the sources' isotope values were measured separately in each region. The
model and data are exactly as in MixSIAR's vignette; only the fitting call changes,
`run_pfn()` in place of `write_JAGS_model()` and `run_model()`.

## The data

```{r load, eval = TRUE}
mix <- load_mix_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "wolves_consumer.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"), factors = c("Region", "Pack"),
  fac_random = c(TRUE, TRUE), fac_nested = c(FALSE, TRUE), cont_effects = NULL)
source <- load_source_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "wolves_sources.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  source_factors = "Region", conc_dep = FALSE, data_type = "means", mix)
discr <- load_discr_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "wolves_discrimination.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  mix)
mix
source
```

The isospace plot shows the wolves, coloured by region, and each source's mean in
each region after adding the discrimination factor, with ±1 SD:

```{r isospace, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 5}
plot_data(mix = mix, source = source, discr = discr)
```

## Fitting the model

Residual * Process error and MixSIAR's uninformative prior, as in MixSIAR's
vignette. The network for this error structure is downloaded the first time it is
needed (about 36 MB) and cached.

```{r fit}
time <- system.time(
  fit <- run_pfn(mix, source, discr, alpha.prior = 1,
                 resid_err = TRUE, process_err = TRUE)
)
fit
```

The fit took `r num(time[["elapsed"]], 1)` seconds.

## Results

`output_pfn()` takes MixSIAR's `output_options` list. It prints the summary
statistics, with MixSIAR's row names, and draws a posterior density plot for the
global diet, each effect and each parameter (here shown, not saved):

```{r output, results = "hide", fig.show = "hide"}
out <- output_pfn(fit, mix, source,
                  output_options = list(summary_save = FALSE, plot_post_save_pdf = FALSE))
```

```{r summary-table}
knitr::kable(round(summary_table(fit), 3))
```

```{r result-plots, fig.height = 4}
out$plots$global
out$plots$Region
```

```{r pack-plot, fig.height = 6}
out$plots$Pack
```

```{r sd-plots, fig.height = 3, fig.width = 3.5, out.width = "48%", fig.show = "hold"}
out$plots$Region.SD
out$plots$Pack.SD
```

Each of these is a **marginal** posterior. The network gives each proportion's
posterior on its own, not joint draws, so the marginal means of one diet need not
sum to exactly 1, and sums, differences or ratios of proportions cannot be computed
from the output.

## Comparison with MixSIAR

```{r reference}
ref <- mixsiar_reference("wolves")
cmp <- compare_mixsiar(fit, ref$draws, ref$summary)
```

MixSIAR `r if (ok) ref$info$mixsiar` fitted the same model with
`r if (ok) ref$info$chains` chains of `r if (ok) format(ref$info$chain_length, big.mark = ",")`
iterations (burn-in `r if (ok) format(ref$info$burn, big.mark = ",")`, thinned by
`r if (ok) ref$info$thin`), a run of about `r num(ref$info$minutes / 60, 1)` hours that
was needed for the Region SD to converge (largest Gelman-Rubin diagnostic
`r num(ref$info$max_psrf, 3)`). MixSIARPFN took `r num(time[["elapsed"]], 1)` seconds.

The table gives both posteriors' means, SDs and 95% intervals, and the Wasserstein-1
distance between them (W1: how far, on average, one posterior's mass has to move to
match the other, on the proportion scale; MixSIAR's draws for the SDs and residual
multipliers were not saved, so those rows have no W1):

```{r compare-table}
show <- transform(cmp, `MixSIARPFN 95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", pfn_q2.5, pfn_q97.5),
                  `MixSIAR 95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", mixsiar_q2.5, mixsiar_q97.5),
                  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = show$name,
  `MixSIARPFN mean` = round(show$pfn_mean, 3), `MixSIAR mean` = round(show$mixsiar_mean, 3),
  `MixSIARPFN SD` = round(show$pfn_sd, 3), `MixSIAR SD` = round(show$mixsiar_sd, 3),
  show[c("MixSIARPFN 95% CI", "MixSIAR 95% CI")], W1 = round(show$w1, 3),
  check.names = FALSE))
```

The posterior densities side by side, for the global diet, the regions and the
packs:

```{r compare-global, fig.height = 3}
plot_compare(fit, ref$draws, block = "global")
```

```{r compare-region, fig.height = 5}
plot_compare(fit, ref$draws, block = "Region")
```

```{r compare-pack, fig.height = 8}
plot_compare(fit, ref$draws, block = "Pack")
```

And every proportion's posterior mean and SD against MixSIAR's:

```{r compare-means, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_compare(fit, ref$draws, type = "means")
```

```{r numbers, include = FALSE}
diet <- cmp[!is.na(cmp$w1), ]
stat <- function(b, f) f(diet[diet$block == b, ])
gap <- function(d) mean(abs(d$pfn_mean - d$mixsiar_mean))
worst <- diet[which.max(abs(diet$pfn_mean - diet$mixsiar_mean)), ]
```

**What this shows.** For the global and region diets, MixSIARPFN's posterior means
differ from MixSIAR's by `r num(stat("global", gap))` and `r num(stat("Region", gap))`
on average, against MixSIAR posterior SDs of about
`r num(stat("global", function(d) mean(d$mixsiar_sd)))` and
`r num(stat("Region", function(d) mean(d$mixsiar_sd)))`, and its posteriors are a
little wider (median SD ratio `r num(stat("global", function(d) median(d$sd_ratio)))`
and `r num(stat("Region", function(d) median(d$sd_ratio)))`). The pack diets differ
more. Most pack means are close (median difference
`r num(stat("Pack", function(d) median(abs(d$pfn_mean - d$mixsiar_mean))))`), but
MixSIARPFN's pack posteriors are about twice as wide (median SD ratio
`r num(stat("Pack", function(d) median(d$sd_ratio)))`) and a few means are far off,
the largest being `r if (ok) sub("^p\\.", "", worst$name)` (`r num(worst$pfn_mean)`
against `r num(worst$mixsiar_mean)`). The Region and Pack SDs and the residual
multipliers are also wider. For a dataset like this, with many small levels,
MixSIARPFN gives a quick first answer, and a MixSIAR run is the more precise one when
time allows.
